BEAC Annual Equity ConferenceChampaign, Illinois

01 · Executive summary

BEAC has the foundation for a great conference. It needs someone to bring it together.

The situation

A strong event with years of history

Past conferences, speakers, sponsors, attendee lists and marketing materials all exist. The next conference is set for late April 2027 in Champaign, and the BEAC team is ready to build it.

The challenge

A big vision, and no one running production

The vision is clear, but no one turns it into deliverables, owners and dates. Information arrives late, work lands on whoever is closest, and too much gets done at the last minute.

The approach

One lead, one plan, one look

I lead the production: a master plan the whole team works from, marketing that starts on time, and conference materials that look like one professional event.

“

A finished conference program isn't one design job. It's six coordinated steps, and the design can only be as on time as the information behind it.

02 · What BEAC needs

Five priorities for the next conference.

Drawn from the handoff with Frederick Mountain Group and BEAC's own materials.

01

Turn the vision into a production plan

A complete list of what the conference needs, who owns each piece, and when it's due.

How I'll solve itA master plan and deliverables list in the first three weeks, approved by Patrick.

02

Stop the last-minute scramble

Speaker bios, sponsor logos and approvals have arrived late in past years, and work fell to whoever was closest.

How I'll solve itClear owners, content deadlines and a weekly check-in, so problems surface early.

03

Start promotion on time

The call for presenters should open before December 1. Speakers, sponsors and registration follow from it.

How I'll solve itA marketing calendar built backward from April 2027. The speaker lead runs the call for presenters; I promote it.

04

Look like one professional event

The website, emails, social posts, program and signage should feel like a single, polished conference.

How I'll solve itOne visual identity, directed across every channel and every printed piece.

05

Systems that save the team time

Registration, payments and files are spread across several tools, and online giving is down while the Bloomerang account is disabled.

How I'll solve itA new conference-ready website with registration, membership and giving in one place, and one home for files.

03 · My role

Conference Project Lead & Creative Director.

Patrick keeps every executive decision. I make sure the work behind those decisions is organized, assigned, produced and delivered.

Workstream 1

Lead the plan

Turn the vision into a production plan and keep the whole team moving on it.

  • Master timeline and deliverables list
  • Owners, deadlines and approvals for every piece
  • Weekly 30-minute check-in
  • The Conference Command Center

Workstream 2

Direct marketing & design

Promote the conference from save-the-date to thank-you, with one consistent look.

  • Promoting the call for presenters and speakers
  • Email campaigns and social media
  • Program, signage, sponsor brochure, slides
  • Post-conference survey and recap

Workstream 3

Make the systems work

Make sure the tools behind the conference save time instead of creating it.

  • Registration pages and forms
  • Membership and online giving
  • One home for files and records
  • The new conference-ready website

I own the coordination system, not every task in it. Each person keeps their own work, with a clear handoff.

Every deliverable follows the same six steps.

Agree on what's needed and who approves it.

02

Organize

03

04

Design, write and build.

05

Review

Feedback and sign-off.

06

Deliver

Publish, print or launch, then archive.

06 · Ways to engage

Two ways to work together. Both start with the Blueprint.

The Blueprint is a 2–3 week planning phase that maps every deliverable, owner and date. BEAC keeps it, whichever option comes next.

Membership

Join the coalition working for Black students and educators.

When you make a tax-deductible donation to BEAC, you become a member for one year, and part of a diverse community of passionate people working together to make a difference in education.

Join as an individualJoin as an organization
Unrestricted supportYour membership funds BEAC's advocacy, research and services in education.
Patrick Rice, Ph.D.President, BEAC

A call to action

Dear friends, colleagues and supporters:

Black students represent the worst case for receiving a quality education in the U.S. According to the Brookings Institute, Black students are less likely to have access to advanced classes, and face unfavorable teacher-student ratios, higher suspension rates and lower graduation rates. Sadly, many nonprofit educational organizations lack staff diversity and have missed the target in advancing issues unique to Black students.

Please consider becoming a change agent and join the fight to stop the injustices for Black students by becoming a member of BEAC.

Yours in the struggle,
Patrick Rice, Ph.D., President

BEAC Annual Equity Conference

Two days for the people who move equity in education forward.

Keynotes, breakout sessions and real conversation for educators, school leaders, board members and advocates working to improve outcomes for Black students and educators.

Late April 2027Champaign, IllinoisEducators · Leaders · Advocates
Get registration updatesSubmit a proposal

Who it's for

Everyone who shapes a Black student's school day

Teachers, principals, superintendents, school board members, higher-ed faculty, parents and community partners.

What you'll leave with

Practices you can use on Monday

Research-based strategies for culturally relevant instruction, social-emotional learning, and recruiting and retaining Black educators.

Why it matters

The work is urgent

BEAC's national report documents how workplace racism drives Black teachers out of the profession. The conference is where districts learn to keep them.
